title: The Present Indicative Active — Second and Third
subtitle: moneō / regō. Long ē versus short ĭ as theme vowel.
objectives: Conjugate second- and third-conjugation verbs in the present active.
Translate sentences with mixed conjugation verbs.
Recognize verb conjugation by infinitive ending.

sections.heading: Second and third conjugations
sections.body:
The second conjugation has infinitives in -ēre (long e): monēre (to warn). Theme vowel: -ē-.

Second conjugation:
  moneō, monēs, monet, monēmus, monētis, monent

The third conjugation has infinitives in -ĕre (short e): regere (to rule). Theme vowel: -ĭ- (short i), which disappears or changes in some forms.

Third conjugation:
  regō, regis, regit, regimus, regitis, regunt

Caesar writes: mīlitēs dūcit. — He leads the soldiers.
Cicero writes: populum Rōmānum regunt. — They rule the Roman people.

items.prompt: Conjugate videō (to see, 2nd conj.) in all six persons.
items.answer: videō, vidēs, videt, vidēmus, vidētis, vident

items.prompt: Conjugate mittō (to send, 3rd conj.) in all six persons.
items.answer: mittō, mittis, mittit, mittimus, mittitis, mittunt

items.prompt: How do you distinguish 2nd from 3rd conjugation?
items.answer: 2nd has -ē- theme vowel and infinitive in -ēre (long e); 3rd has -ĭ- and infinitive in -ĕre (short e).

lesson_completion.criteria: Mark complete when you can conjugate moneō and regō and distinguish their theme vowels.
